articles.title: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring
articles.summary: Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan.The agreement…
articles.body: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Conceptual image of the system (Credit: NYK Line) Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan. The agreement, signed on November 25, brings together NYK Line, MUFG Bank, Nagoya Electric Works, ArkEdge Space, Shimizu Corporation, the City of Yokohama, Yokohama-Kawasaki International Port Corporation and Yokohama Port Corporation. The collaboration will advance the True Emission Eye - Maritime project, which aims to develop technology for measuring, visualizing and quantifying greenhouse gas emissions from ships at a distance. The project will conduct measurements on actual vessels at Yokohama Port to assess the technology's accuracy, while examining system specifications, potential applications and opportunities for future commercial deployment. The technology is being developed to complement existing methods of estimating vessel emissions based on fuel type and consumption, providing a means of directly measuring emissions from outside ships. The system uses optical observation technology that exploits the ability of gases, including carbon dioxide, to absorb and emit light at specific wavelengths. Data obtained from vessel exhaust observations is combined with physical parameters, including distance to the ship and weather conditions, to calculate emissions. Testing has already been conducted at experimental facilities and on NYK Group vessels, both at berth and underway. At Yokohama Port, the project has captured infrared images of ship exhaust from observation points including Osanbashi Pier and the Yokohama Bay Bridge Skywalk. The images are being compared and analyzed against vessel data to evaluate the technology. The partners will continue conducting measurements under different conditions to improve the accuracy of the system, while also examining fixed-point monitoring at ports. The project will also assess the technical requirements for satellite-based observations of ship emissions and explore the potential integration of satellite measurements with ground-based data. The eight organizations aim to bring the technology into practical use to improve transparency in vessel emissions reporting and support decarbonization across the shipping and port sectors.

November 25, 2026 (Credit: Royal Wagenborg) Wärtsilä has secured an order to supply engines for four new 14,000-deadweight-tonne general cargo vessels being built for Dutch shipowner Royal Wagenborg, extending its involvement in the company's EasyMax 2.0 fleet renewal programme. The four vessels will be equipped with Wärtsilä 25 engines, following the selection of the same engine type for the first two EasyMax 2.0 ships in 2025, the Finnish technology group announced on November 25. The new vessels are being constructed at Royal Niestern Sander shipyard in the Netherlands, with deliveries of Wärtsilä equipment scheduled to begin in 2027. The engine order was booked in the fourth quarter of 2026, although its financial value was not disclosed. The Wärtsilä 25 features a modular architecture designed to enable future conversion to alternative low- and zero-carbon fuels as they become commercially available. Each engine will also be equipped with Wärtsilä's NOx Reducer (NOR) emissions after-treatment system, which uses selective catalytic reduction technology to reduce nitrogen oxide emissions. The engine selection forms part of Wagenborg's EasyMax 2.0 design, which focuses on fuel efficiency, operational flexibility and reduced emissions. Wagenborg operates a fleet of more than 160 vessels, with Wärtsilä equipment installed on over half of them. The companies also maintain a long-term service agreement covering engines and propulsion systems across Wagenborg's fleet. The latest order follows the use of Wärtsilä 32 engines on the shipowner's previous EasyMax vessels.

articles.title: Most Large Fuel Tankers Now Ship ‘Dirty’ Crude, Upending Trading
articles.summary: A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated.

Join the leading maritime news network Photo: Avigator Thailand/Shutterstock By Weilun Soon Nov 25, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated. Less than a quarter of the world’s 542 long-range 2, or LR2, tankers are currently transporting “clean” cargoes such as jet fuel, naphtha and diesel as of this week, according to Signal Ocean data. The vessels have cargo holds that are coated to transport refined fuels, and have to undergo an expensive cleaning process to return to the trade once they ship “dirty” crude oil. The shift in use of the LR2 fleet comes as crude flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz. A system of shuttling tankers and ship-to-ship transfers has helped exports from the Persian Gulf recover to pre-war levels, boosting freight rates and prompting charterers to tap smaller vessels to meet demand. Benchmark earnings for very-large crude carriers have soared, in turn enabling smaller-sized tankers — including Aframaxes, which are the crude-focused equivalent of LR2s, able to hold about 750,000 barrels — to command far higher fees. And an LR2 that dirties up can charge Aframax earnings. Shipping executives often look at how many LR2s are switching to plan on how much they can charge, and how they should deploy their tankers around the world. Even though the LR2 fleet has grown 12% since January last year and clean-fuel shipments have fallen due to the US-Iran war, the increased switching to crude has helped put a floor underneath the fees they can command to carry oil products. “Tracking LR2 employment between clean and dirty trades is becoming as important as monitoring the size of the fleet itself,” Signal analysts Maria Bertzeletou and Georgios Sakellariou said. The switching of LR2s started last year as traders sought to store more crude on vessels at sea, but accelerated in the initial phase of the Iran War from the end of February, when refineries in the Middle East were attacked by the Islamic Republic — reducing the need for clean tankers, Sakellariou said. Read More: Oil Tankers Get ‘Dirty’ Ditching Fuels for Crude as Rates Boom A lot of the processing plants in the region remain unavailable, reducing the need for products tankers. About 1.7 million out of the more than 9 million barrels a day of refining capacity is currently offline in the Middle East, RBC Capital Markets analysts including Christopher Louney and Helima Croft wrote in a note this week. Around 1 million barrels a day of that potentially needs months to repair, they said. Charterers are turning to smaller product tankers, with the share of LR2s in transporting fuels falling to just 12% between July and September, from almost 18% a year earlier, Signal data show. Meanwhile, a benchmark freight index reflecting daily LR2 earnings from the Mediterranean to Asia increased more than five-fold, while another from the Middle East to Europe jumped more than 10-fold in the year through end-September. © 2026 Bloomberg L.P. Join the leading maritime news network On 24 November 2026, Windcat signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for the second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) in the Innovation Series. The contract follows the order for the first vessel , with an option for five more, signed in November last year. Sound basis The MP-ASV is an entirely new type of vessel designed to support operations in the offshore energy industry . Its design draws heavily on Damen’s experience in the design and construction of Commissioning Services Operations Vessels (CSOVs). This includes the Elevation Series CSOVs, developed together by Damen and Windcat. The first vessel in the Elevation Series, Windcat Rotterdam , was presented with the KNVTS Ship of the Year Award at this year’s Maritime Awards Gala. The MP-ASV takes the proven capabilities of the Elevation Series CSOVs and builds on them further. Extended capabilities The MP-ASVs build on these capabilities in a number of ways, including with their 102 x 20 metre hull and its 750m 2 deck space. The MP-ASV is able to assist and operate in all offshore energy markets, including cable repair, flotel functions, offshore wind and ROV assistance. Additionally, the vessel is fitted with 111 cabins, allowing up to 190 persons on board. The vessel features an offshore crane which can be used as a 150-tonne subsea crane, or as a 15-tonne 3D motion-compensated crane. The vessel can also be fitted with remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). The vessels are being equipped with a DP2+ system holding DNV CBS and CBT class notations, which cover a wider scope of redundant closed bus-ties system arrangements, for enhanced fault tolerance. The DP system features additional tunnel thrusters fore and aft to provide increased redundancy for safe operations in remote offshore locations. Access is via a 3D motion-compensated gangway with two exchangeable tips, one for short connections used in the wind industry and one capable of long continuous connections. Prepared for efficiency The MP-ASVs will be outfitted with a battery system to enable peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing. This will enable highly efficient operations, for example when in DP mode. Like the Windcat CSOVs, a key feature of the Innovation Series vessels is the integration of low-carbon fuels . Hence a dual fuel hydrogen auxiliary genset is installed, and the three main generator sets are of the next generation Evolve generator sets from ABC, which allow for a range of low-emission possibilities. These engines can operate on liquid fuels such as biodiesel and HVO, on dual fuel with pilot injection of liquid fuel, or on 100% gas using spark ignition. High offshore comfort level The design of the vessel is also highly focused on comfort for the up to 190 personnel onboard. Measures include well-thought-out routing, use of high-quality materials and aesthetically appealing accommodation. The aim is to make crew and personnel feel at home during extended periods of up to 150 days offshore, due to her extended fuel capacity. Strength-to-strength Damen Sales Director Joost van der Weiden says, “We are delighted to receive this second MP-ASV order from Windcat. The cooperation that began with our development of the Elevation Series continues to grow in strength. With the Innovation Series we mutually have developed a vessel that will further enhance Windcat’s capabilities to support its clients in the offshore energy industry in the years ahead.” Windcat Managing Director Willem van der Wel says: “The decision to order a second MP-ASV reflects our confidence in this new vessel concept and our ambition to further strengthen our position in the offshore energy market. By combining the capabilities of a multi-purpose support vessel with high-quality offshore accommodation, we are creating a versatile solution that responds to the evolving needs of our customers. articles.body: Petronas Names ‘World's First’ Nearshore FLNG Facility Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Petronas) Petronas has officially named its third floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility, PFLNG TIGA, at Samsung Heavy Industries' shipyard in South Korea, ahead of its planned deployment to Malaysia and start-up in the third quarter of 2027. Described by Petronas as the world's first nearshore FLNG facility, PFLNG TIGA is currently under construction at the shipyard on Geoje Island and will be deployed to Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysia. The facility is designed to produce 2 million tonnes of LNG annually and measures 281 metres in length, 64 metres in width and 32 metres in depth. PFLNG TIGA will become the third floating LNG facility developed by Petronas , expanding its portfolio of facilities designed for shallow-water, deepwater and nearshore environments. The new facility is intended to support the development and commercialisation of gas resources while strengthening Malaysia's LNG supply capabilities. Petronas said the addition would provide greater flexibility in bringing gas resources to market and meeting regional and international demand. The company has been active in the LNG industry for more than four decades, with PFLNG TIGA representing another addition to its integrated LNG portfolio.

November 25, 2026 © Miha Creative / Adobe Stock Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East. Brent crude futures LCOc1 declined 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 slipped 62 cents, or 0.8%, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday. "Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage. On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery ‌and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast ‌that ⁠also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude. A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said. US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. API/S Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average. "Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said. Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya. "However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said. A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media. On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday. articles.body: Windcat Expands Offshore Fleet with Second Damen Multi-Purpose Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Windcat) Windcat has signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for a second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) under its Innovation Series, expanding its planned fleet of vessels designed for offshore energy operations. The agreement, signed on November 24, follows Windcat's initial order in November 2025 for the first vessel in the series, which included an option for five additional units. The new MP-ASV design builds on the companies' earlier collaboration on the Elevation Series commissioning service operations vessels (CSOVs), incorporating additional capabilities for offshore wind, subsea cable repair, offshore accommodation and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) support. The vessels will measure 102 meters in length and 20 meters in width, with approximately 750 square meters of deck space and 111 cabins accommodating up to 190 personnel. Each MP-ASV will feature an offshore crane capable of operating as a 150-tonne subsea crane or a 15-tonne three-dimensional motion-compensated crane, alongside provisions for ROV installation. Personnel transfers will be supported by a 3D motion-compensated gangway with interchangeable tips designed for short connections in offshore wind operations and longer continuous connections. The vessels will also feature a DP2+ dynamic positioning system with DNV CBS and CBT class notations, incorporating additional bow and stern tunnel thrusters to improve redundancy during offshore operations. The propulsion and power arrangement will include a battery system for peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing, together with a dual-fuel hydrogen auxiliary generator. Three main generator sets supplied by ABC will feature its Evolve technology, designed to accommodate different fuel options, including biodiesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), dual-fuel operation and gas. The MP-ASVs are designed for extended offshore deployments of up to 150 days, supported by increased fuel capacity and accommodation facilities intended for prolonged stays at sea. The Innovation Series builds on Damen and Windcat's Elevation Series partnership, which includes the Windcat Rotterdam, named KNVTS Ship of the Year at the 2026 Maritime Awards Gala.

articles.title: NextGeo Gets $12.7M Offshore Survey Job for Spain-France Hydrogen Link
articles.summary: Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting…
articles.body: NextGeo Gets $12.7M Offshore Survey Job for Spain-France Hydrogen Link Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting Spain and France. The contract covers an integrated survey campaign along an approximately 366-kilometre offshore corridor between Barcelona, Spain, and Fos-sur-Mer, France. The scope includes geophysical, geotechnical and UXO surveys, grab sampling, remotely operated vehicle (ROV) inspections and surveys of crossings with existing subsea infrastructure. The data collected will be used to characterise seabed and sub-seabed conditions to support the planning and design of the future pipeline. NextGeo will deploy two dedicated vessels for the offshore operations, which are expected to begin by the end of 2026. The campaign is currently scheduled for completion between the end of the second quarter and the beginning of the third quarter of 2027, depending on any additional work requested during execution. The BarMar pipeline forms part of H2med, a cross-border initiative designed to connect hydrogen networks in the Iberian Peninsula with northwestern Europe. The project is being developed by BarMar S.A.S., whose shareholders are NaTran, Enagás and Teréga. H2med is included on the European Union's list of Projects of Common Interest, with BarMar providing the planned maritime hydrogen transport connection between Spain and France. The award marks NextGeo's first contract with BarMar, expanding its offshore survey activities into hydrogen infrastructure development.

November 25, 2026 © DigitalPenTH / Adobe Stock Maersk has ordered 12 ultra-large container ships scheduled for delivery in 2030 and 2031, which will become the biggest vessels in its fleet, a company spokesperson said on Tuesday. The vessels, each able to carry 24,000 twenty-foot containers, will be equipped with dual-fuel engines capable of operating on conventional bunker fuel or liquefied gas, Maersk said in an emailed statement. Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) and The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI) are proud to announce that both companies are now 100% employee owned through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), marking an important milestone for the two naval architecture and marine engineering firms. For Gregory W. Beers, P.E., and Cory C. Wood, who founded BHGI in 1995 and later established TSGI in 2010, the transition represents the continuation of a vision that began more than three decades ago: to build the most well-respected naval architecture and marine engineering firms in the industry. Gregory and Cory have spent decades building BHGI and TSGI with a vision that extends well beyond their own leadership. Through careful planning, the development of strong management teams, and a continued investment in their employees, they have positioned both firms to become multigenerational leaders in the naval architecture and marine engineering industry. The transition to employee ownership is a significant step in securing that future, ensuring that the companies they founded continue to grow and succeed for generations to come. While ownership has changed, both firms will continue operating much as they have for years. Gregory and Cory will remain at the forefront of both companies, providing leadership and direction alongside their established management teams. Clients can continue to expect the same level of service and technical expertise from the employees they’ve come to know and trust over the years. BHGI’s History BHGI traces its origins back to 1993, when Gregory and Cory, along with Andy Tyska of Bristol Marine and another fellow student at the University of Michigan Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Department set out to design a passenger vessel while still in school. Their first design, the STAR OF SAUGATUCK II , marked an early milestone for the firm and is still operating on the Kalamazoo River in Southwest Michigan. Building on that early initiative, the group formally incorporated BHGI in 1995, and the firm has continued to grow in Bristol, Rhode Island, ever since. Over the years, BHGI has developed into a close-knit team of 19, maintaining a hands-on, collaborative working environment. Today, the engineering team is led by Daniel P. Eling, P.E. For more than three decades, BHGI has been guided by a set of core values established early on by Greg and Cory. Those values continue to shape the firm’s work today and center on technical excellence, attention to detail, a strong focus on clients, engineering ethics, professionalism, and responsibility. TSGI’s History In 2010, Gregory and Cory formed The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI), a sister company to BHGI located in Houston, Texas. The company was established when Gregory and Cory purchased the assets of Shearer & Assoc., Inc. from Edward L. Shearer, P.E., its founder and president. The three had heard of one another through industry connections and eventually met at a SNAME convention. That encounter led to further discussions, and ultimately the formation of TSGI. The “Shearer” name has long been associated with the inland marine industry, reflecting both Ed’s contributions to naval architecture and his family’s multigenerational barge line. When TSGI was established, it brought together Ed’s years of experience at Shearer & Associates, Inc. and the naval architecture and marine engineering expertise Gregory and Cory had developed at BHGI. Ed remains involved as a Principal Naval Architect. Today, TSGI provides marine engineering services to clients in the inland and offshore marine industries. The firm offers many of the same services as BHGI, along with additional services suited to its Houston location, including marine surveying and OSHA-compliant maritime gear certification support. As TSGI continued to grow, Joshua S. Sebastian, P.E., joined the firm in 2013, bringing five years of engineering experience at BHGI, along with his nine-year background as an officer in the U.S. Coast Guard. He relocated to Texas to serve as Engineering Manager, as part of Gregory and Cory’s plan to build TSGI with the same technical and cultural approach used at BHGI. In 2022, Joshua stepped into the role of Vice President – Operations, with Senior Naval Architect Harrison C. Brann, P.E., stepping into the role of Engineering Manager. Over 15 years, TSGI has grown into another close-knit team of 19. Under Joshua and Harrison’s leadership, TSGI has continued to grow while maintaining the same approach and core principles established at BHGI. Today, the firm remains dedicated to serving vessels that operate on the inland waterways and continuing the tradition established by its namesake. Leadership and Employee Ownership With the ESOP now in place, Gregory will serve as Chairman and President, Cory as Vice Chairman, and Joshua as Vice President of both BHGI and TSGI. The engineering teams will continue under the direction of Daniel at BHGI and Harrison at TSGI, both as Engineering Managers. What began as a design effort in a college house has grown into two established firms, each built in a steady and deliberate way. Over the years, Gregory and Cory have built management teams that allow BHGI and TSGI to grow without losing sight of the values on which they were founded. Now, with ownership in the hands of their employees, both firms will continue the work they were built to do, guided by the same commitment to their clients, their profession, and a shared belief that their purpose is to create. To mark the transition to employee ownership, BHGI and TSGI recognized employees who were with the firms at the time as “Plank Owners,” a nautical term traditionally used for members of a vessel’s commissioning crew. Each employee received a commemorative “Built to Last” challenge coin featuring the “Plank Owner” designation. Both offices also have permanent “Plank Owner” plaques on display, recognizing these employees and their place in the companies’ history. For BHGI and TSGI, employee ownership is another part of what it means to be built to last. About BHGI Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) is a naval architecture and marine engineering firm located in Bristol, Rhode Island. Founded in 1995, BHGI provides vessel design, engineering, and consulting services to commercial and government clients throughout the marine industry. To learn more, you can visit our website: http://bristolharborgroup.com . About TSGI The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI) is a naval architecture and marine engineering firm located in Houston, Texas. Established in 2010, TSGI provides naval architecture, marine engineering, marine surveying, and related consulting services to clients in the inland and offshore marine industries. To learn more, you can visit our website: http://shearer-group.com. articles.title: Maersk and ONE Eye Landmark Global North-South Shipping Alliance
articles.summary: The formation of container shipping’s first global liner alliance covering the north-south trades appears to be taking shape, The Loadstar has learned.
articles.body: Advertise Forum Jobs Subscribe Grab a Seat at the Captain’s Table Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe. Join the leading maritime news network Containers are seen on the Maersk's Triple-E giant container ship Majestic Maersk, one of the world's largest container ships, next to cranes at the APM Terminals in the port of Algeciras, Spain January 20, 2023. REUTERS/Jon Nazca/File Photo By Nils Roche (The Loadstar) – The formation of container shipping’s first global liner alliance covering the north-south trades appears to be taking shape, The Loadstar has learned. Container lines have traditionally treated the north-south trades as a set of separate marriages, on the assumption that the right partner depends on the trade. However, according to sources in Asia, Maersk and Ocean Network Express (ONE) are working to develop a vessel-sharing agreement (VSA) covering the trades globally, rather than lane by lane. The Loadstar has approached both carriers for comment but has yet to receive a formal response, and the form the VDSA would take is unclear. Nonetheless, if confirmed it would be the first VSA of its kind – and its logic rests on ONE’s fleet, according to our provisional analysis below. Their respective groupings, the Gemini Cooperation for Maersk and Premier Alliance for ONE, stop at east-west trades, while north-south has remained a patchwork of classic VSAs, where each carrier’s slots follow the ships it provides, and an agreement rarely covers more than two or three services. Why not Hapag-Lloyd? The obvious choice of partner for Maersk would be Hapag-Lloyd, its Gemini compatriot – but two things rule it out. The first is that CSAV owns 30% of it and sits in the shareholder pact that controls more than 70% of the carrier, so combining West Coast South America networks would join two incumbents serving the same Chilean and Peruvian exporters. In that context, it is worth noting that Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd do not cooperate on any of their respective Asia-WC South America services – according to Xeneta’s eeSea liner database, Maersk operates two standalone strings, the AC1 and AC3, while Hapag-Lloyd’s three offerings are run in cooperation with MSC, HMM, and ONE. Secondly, Hapag-Lloyd has relatively few ships coming – its orderbook is 19% of its fleet, the lowest of the eight largest carriers, on trades where Far East–Latin America capacity grew 14% in a year. ONE poses fewer of those problems. On Far East–WC South America, for example, Linerlytica puts Maersk at 16.1% of weekly capacity and ONE at 9%; together a quarter of the trade, ahead of CMA CGM and MSC, from two carriers whose customers overlap less. The ships are the point ONE has the fleet those trades are moving towards. Alphaliner puts 36% of its operated capacity in ships of 10,000–15,100 teu, against 14% at Maersk. Of the 55 ships ONE has on order, 29 – representing 60% of the total 647,000 teu expected – fall in the same bracket. Linerlytica puts the average ship on Far East–Latin America already at 10,032 teu. However, only 10 of ONE’s 62 ships in that class currently work Latin American routes. Under the classic formula, ships buy slots, so tonnage converts directly into share. A global partner gives ONE’s newbuilds work without ONE building Latin American and African franchises alone. Maersk, whose next order according to Linerlytica is for 24,000 teu ships, would thus get mid-size capacity without ordering it. What it will probably look like “Global” may describe the scope more than the mechanics. North-south shippers pay for direct calls, Brazil reserves feeder legs for Brazilian-flag operators, and Mexico’s ports do little relay business. That points to core loops on one carrier’s ships where its fleet fits, and shared loops where the ship mix demands it, rather than a Gemini-style hub network. The obstacles are real. Hapag-Lloyd sits alongside ONE in several of these consortia, so the deal means reordering them with Maersk’s own Gemini partner, and a quarter of Asia–WC South America capacity will interest regulators in Chile and Peru. And similar disentanglements will be necessary on other north-south trades: for example, Maersk continues to cooperate with CMA CGM on Asia-West Africa services. And although there were rumours that that cooperation might be coming to an end, they have subsided for now. The quay question… …will be where ONE’s 13,724 teu newbuilds are deployed in 2027. The industry has assumed north-south partners must be chosen trade by trade. A Maersk–ONE framework tests a different premise: that the scarce input is the right ship, and a carrier holding them can be a partner almost everywhere.
